procedure.status: DRAFTED — pending Founder review and human legal notification-law conclusions

definitionsOperationalNotLegal.securityIncident: An event that may compromise confidentiality, integrity, or availability of The Back Half systems, credentials, or data. Operational term only.
definitionsOperationalNotLegal.privacyEvent: An event that may involve unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or loss of personal information of Architects, prospects, or operators. Operational term only.
definitionsOperationalNotLegal.suspectedBreach: A privacy/security event that might later be a legally notifiable breach. Agents must not conclude that a legal 'breach' has or has not occurred.
personalInformationInScopeExamples: Billing information processed by Stripe (card data is not stored by The Back Half application; Stripe is the processor)
Journey answers and Lumina transcripts (first-party; Lumina does not call OpenAI)
Analytics events tied to a userId
definitionsOperationalNotLegal.clockStart: Michelle records detectionTime (first credible signal) and confirmationTime (Imani confirms a security/privacy event, or Founder/counsel later confirms a legal breach). Notification clocks, if any, are determined only by human legal counsel. Agents do not start or stop statutory clocks.

severityForPrivacySecurityEvents.rule: Reuse OS SEV-1 through SEV-4. Do not invent a second severity scale. Material security/privacy incidents are SEV-1 examples in the OS.

SEV-1.name: CRITICAL
privacySecurityExamples: Confirmed or highly likely unauthorized access to Architect personal data
Material data-loss or destructive event involving personal data
Vendor notice that The Back Half production project is in a confirmed unauthorized-access window
notify: Nia if participant impact or public surfaces
Human legal expert if required — Founder engages

SEV-2.name: HIGH
privacySecurityExamples: Contained exposure affecting a meaningful cohort, not yet confirmed as broadly acquired
Vendor notice of possible but unconfirmed project impact
Single-account compromise with personal data at risk
Misdirected communication containing another Architect's personal information
notify: Founder if material launch, reputational, financial, or reserved

SEV-3.name: MODERATE
privacySecurityExamples: Failed intrusion with no data access
Single support message that included a secret, already redacted, no further exposure
Vendor generic advisory with no indication The Back Half is in scope

SEV-4.name: LOW
privacySecurityExamples: Phishing attempt with no credential use
Public rumor with no corroborating evidence after Imani triage

1_detection.name: Detection
1_detection.owner: Any operator who first sees a credible signal; Michelle records; Imani triages technical truth.
sources: Row 61 probes, launch_ops_errors, Row 151 Launch Health / Founder Attention
Row 153 support form, support@, category PRIVACY or TECHNICAL, P1 security language
Row 83 social reports of exposure, credential stuffing, impersonation, or alleged company breach
Vendor status pages and vendor-to-Founder security emails (Vercel, Supabase, Stripe, Google Workspace, OpenAI, GitHub, Cloudflare/registrar, Meta/Instagram, TikTok)
Unusual Stripe Radar/disputes, auth failure spikes, admin-console access anomalies
Founder or operator observation of unauthorized posts, DNS change, or missing MFA
intakeRules: Do not request passwords, OTP, full PAN, CVV, or recovery codes from the reporter.
If an Architect already sent a secret: redact, do not repeat, escalate to Imani, do not ask them to resend the secret (Row 153).
Privacy allegations against the company are not ordinary CX. Michelle routes to Imani + Founder. Do not investigate publicly.
Attorney, regulator, or government contact: preserve, do not reply substantively, Michelle surfaces Founder immediately. No legal@ mailbox.
Create or attach a Row 153 ticket when the signal came from an Architect or public support path. Do not open a second informal tracker.
1_detection.immediateClassificationDefault: Treat suspected personal-data exposure or credential compromise as SEV-1 or SEV-2 until Imani downgrades with evidence. Do not wait for perfect confirmation to contain obvious ongoing leakage.

2_containment.name: Containment
2_containment.owner: Imani Heartbeat. Michelle notified immediately. Founder notified for SEV-1.
2_containment.authority: OS: incident response — technical containment is Imani independent A (no prior Founder approval). Emergency shutdown is Imani execute, Michelle notify, Founder notify. Public/legal/reputational communication remains Founder-reserved.
allowedWithoutPriorFounderApproval: Disable or isolate a leaking path (feature flag, route disable, pause SMTP send, pause checkout UI, revoke application sessions Imani can revoke in-app)
Rollback to restore approved safe behavior
Emergency shutdown to prevent ongoing harm
Pause social publishing when security-related (Imani/Michelle/Nia per Row 77/83)
Redact secrets in tickets and logs
Block further export/download of the affected store if Imani has an authorized control
requiresFounder: Destructive restore or cutover over production (Row 62)
Rotation of human-owned SaaS passwords, MFA, API keys, and Vercel/Stripe/GitHub/Cloudflare secrets
New public statements, participant notices, regulator notices
forbiddenDuringContainment: Do not restore over production as the first action (Row 62).
Do not wipe logs or rotate in a way that destroys needed evidence before a snapshot is taken.
Do not post a public 'we were breached' statement.
Do not change Cloudflare DNS, Vercel custom-domain, or thebackhalf.org nameservers from agent execution.
Do not weaken authentication to 'keep the site up'.
Do not paste secrets into tickets, chat, git, or this procedure.

3_evidencePreservation.name: Evidence preservation
3_evidencePreservation.owner: Imani preserves technical records. Michelle coordinates the inventory. Nia preserves participant-facing/social evidence. Human legal expert later defines authoritative hold scope. Agents may preserve pending review and may not conclude legal scope or duration (OS legalHoldProtocol).
whatToCapture: Detection time, reporter, channel, ticket ID
Imani's technical timeline (systems, routes, env names — never values)
Affected data categories (not dumps of personal data into git)
Approximate population if knowable (count, not a spreadsheet of Architects in the repo)
Support ticket and social-evidence copies under existing stores (tickets; ops/fab-5/social-evidence/ for social; no secrets in filenames)
Vendor ticket/case IDs and notice timestamps
What containment was applied and by whom
where: ops/fab-5/decision-log.json for material operating decisions and Founder-gated steps (append only when a real incident requires it; this al-169 work does not append a fake incident)
Imani technical notes in authorized ops/admin or launch_ops_errors — sanitized
Do not create a second durable tracker. This JSON is the procedure, not the live incident log.
3_evidencePreservation.personalDataHandling: Copy only the minimum needed to investigate. Do not commit Architect dumps, email lists, Journey answers, or Lumina transcripts to git. Do not expand access during investigation.

6_legalAssessment.name: Legal assessment
6_legalAssessment.owner: Human legal expert for conclusions. Imani identifies technical facts and risk. Michelle escalates and packages facts. Founder engages counsel and accepts/signs.
alwaysEscalateToFounderForCounselWhen: Unauthorized access to or acquisition of personal information is confirmed or reasonably likely
A misdirected communication exposed another person's personal information
A production credential that can read personal data was exposed
A vendor notice says The Back Half is in a confirmed incident window
Public allegation of a company data breach
Any question of whether notice is legally required

factsPackageForCounsel.purpose: Enable counsel to decide notification law. Not a legal conclusion.
fields: systems involved (vendor IDs from the register)

data categories involved (from Privacy Policy categories actually collected — name, email, billing via Stripe, account, purchase/membership, Journey/Lumina if implicated, support contents, analytics identifiers)
whether encryption/hashing applied and whether keys were also compromised (Imani fact, not legal conclusion)
approximate number of individuals if knowable
geography if knowable (country/time zone collected; no DOB; 18+ only)
containment status and whether exposure is ongoing
Privacy Policy Version 1.0 / contact privacy@thebackhalf.org as published — do not rewrite the policy from IR

explicitlyNotConcludedHere: Whether the event is a 'breach of security' under any U.S. state law
Whether CCPA/CPRA, GDPR, or other regimes apply to these facts
Whether vendor contractual notice is due

7_notificationDecisionProcess.name: Notification decision process
7_notificationDecisionProcess.owner: Founder decides after human legal counsel. Michelle runs the process. Nia does not send. Imani does not send. Kimberly Walker (AI) does not send.

steps.step: Imani confirms technical facts and containment status.
Michelle completes the facts package. No legal conclusions in the package.
Michelle surfaces Founder Attention YES / SEV-1. Founder engages qualified human legal counsel. Independent counsel is not currently retained (Row 34). Founder chooses counsel.
Counsel determines whether notice is legally required, to whom, by when, and in what form; and whether contractual vendor/insurer notice is required.

Founder accepts or rejects counsel's recommendation. Record in decision-log.json. This is Founder-reserved public/legal/reputational communication (OS independent E, founderApproval true, humanExpert true).

If notice is required: Founder (or Founder-authorized human sending as The Back Half, never as an agent impersonating Kimberly) sends the counsel-approved text. privacy@ or support@ as counsel directs. Do not invent legal@.
If notice is not required: record counsel's conclusion and the Founder's decision. Continue containment, monitoring, and Architect-specific support using approved templates only.

7_notificationDecisionProcess.defaultWhileAwaitingCounsel: Contain. Do not notify a population 'to be safe' with unapproved legal language. Do not tell the public there was or was not a legally notifiable breach. Individual Architects who already know they were affected (for example a misdirected email) may receive a factual, non-legal acknowledgment through Support: we received this, we are investigating, do not send secrets — no admission beyond facts Imani has confirmed.
noAgentMay: Post social statements about a breach
Rewrite Privacy Policy, Terms, or checkout legal copy as an IR action
